label: <DEL> step of short sequences starting with x that contain o/m/v
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.003% of steps) that fires almost exclusively (99% of mass) at the delimiter step, i.e. when the model is about to output original token 0. About 93% of mass is on sequences whose first token is x (rest mostly first token 1). It is restricted to L = 4..7, peaking at L = 5, and never fires for L = 3 or L >= 8. Within x-first short sequences, activation is driven by o, m and v appearing among the original tokens (v as the last token before <DEL>, m/o two back); the strongest examples (x 1 p o m o, x x k o v, x o m w) contain several of them. Necessary conditions (delimiter, first x, L 4-7) give ~92% recall but only ~1-5% precision, and requiring >= 2 of {o,m,v} with L <= 6 gets precision 0.23 / mass recall 0.68. So the feature is a sharp conjunction on the hidden summary of the sequence that this description captures only in part. It does not fire in the original or copy phases, on other first tokens (apart from a few with first token 1), or on long sequences.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=1 & out_tok=x (+3.04), prev_tok=v (+2.80), orig0=x (+2.66), orig2=o (+2.29), orig2=m (+2.01), orig3=o (+1.86). Lower it: L=8 (-2.92), orig7=- (-2.29), L=9 (-2.22), in_first=0 (-2.06).
